critical_code_review_comments: server.py:6041 — the safe idiom for optional nested dicts is `(d.get('k') or {}).get(...)`, since `d.get('k', {})` returns None when the key EXISTS with value=None. This was a legitimate production-impacting bug that would 500 for ANY coach dashboard call.

clients.tsx — the mixed `useFocusEffect(useCallback(fn, [load]))` pattern is fragile. When load's identity changes while focused, React Navigation's useFocusEffect does not always re-run reliably. Consider using pure `useEffect(load, [filter, showArchived])` + a separate one-off `useFocusEffect` for pull-to-refresh behavior on tab return.

rca_of_issue: Backend RCA: In Python, `dict.get(key, default)` only returns `default` when the key is MISSING. If the key is present with value=None, get() returns None. server.py:5982 explicitly sets `programme_pill = None` when a client has no programme row, so the summary dict has key 'programme_pill' with value None. The Slice 3 buckets code did `s.get('programme_pill', {}).get(...)` — this evaluates to `None.get(...)` → AttributeError → 500. Reproduction: any coach GET on /api/coach/dashboard while at least one client lacks a programme (which was almost all clients). Fix: `(s.get('programme_pill') or {}).get(...)`. Frontend RCA: React Navigation's useFocusEffect only fires the effect on screen focus; while its callback dep can change, in practice on RN Web the effect does NOT re-run reliably when only the callback identity changes but the screen is already focused. So `setFilter('needs_review')` never triggered a fetch. Fix: complement with a plain `useEffect(() => { load(); }, [filter, showArchived])`.
